findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: site_memory, scan_page, site_audit, measure, find_opportunities, ai_visibility, get_fix_pack, request_recrawl, explain_google, check_keyword, local, tracking, check_links, content, technical, llms_txt, schema, robots_txt, sitemap, layout, snippet · Private data: site_memory, backlinks, fix_log, llms_txt, entity · Public sink: watch, measure, backlinks, get_fix_pack, request_recrawl, share, snippet · Destructive: site_memory, find_opportunities, answer_readiness, layout, track_rankings, prioritize_fixes.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: site_memory, scan_page, site_audit, measure, find_opportunities, ai_visibility, get_fix_pack, request_recrawl, explain_google, check_keyword, local, tracking, check_links, content, technical, llms_txt, schema, robots_txt, sitemap, layout, snippet · Private data: site_memory, backlinks, fix_log, llms_txt, entity · Public sink: watch, measure, backlinks, get_fix_pack, request_recrawl, share, snippet · Destructive: site_memory, find_opportunities, answer_readiness, layout, track_rankings, prioritize_fixes

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
